reason: The text contains only a few individually named characters: Sanballat (סַנְבַלַּט) and Tobiah the Ammonite (טוֹבִיָּה הָעַמֹּנִי), who are presented as opponents of prominence and authority organizing resistance to the wall construction. There is a mention of 'Judah' (יְהוּדָה) in a single statement, but this character is part of the leadership deliberations about construction and defense strategy, not a regular person. The 'regular people' doing the actual work (the laborers, builders, and defenders) are mentioned only as collective groups (עָם, הַיְּהוּדִים) without individual names. Therefore, the named characters are not portrayed as regular people, and the regular people are not individually named.
